# Tablekeeper — Stage 2: online booking and combined tables

The stage-1 requirements continue to apply, with the additions below. Numbered section
references such as §5 and §7 refer to `stage-1.md`.

Diners can search, book and manage reservations in a browser. Restaurants can offer
approved pairs of tables for larger parties.

The following screens must be reachable by URL. Other screens must be reachable through
the UI. Server-side and client-side rendering are both permitted.

| Route | Screen |
|---|---|
| `/` | Search and availability grid |
| `/signup` | Signup |
| `/login` | Login |
| `/lookup` | Look up a reservation by reference |

A screen route returns HTML; §3.4's `application/json` convention is about the API, and does
not govern the routes in the table above.

## Competing clients and uncertain outcomes

The UI must handle responses arriving out of order and connections failing after submission.

- If search A starts before search B but finishes after it, the grid, table labels and
  booking form must describe B. A late response must not restore A's results.
- If another client takes a table after the form opens, a `409 table_unavailable` response
  shows `booking-error` and refreshes availability. Preserve the selected form and its
  inputs so the diner can change their choice. Do not show a confirmation for that attempt.
- If a booking response is lost, including after the booking commits, show nonempty
  `booking-uncertain` text, without `booking-error` or a new confirmation. The unchanged
  form must retry with the same idempotency key and body. A successful retry removes the
  uncertainty/error elements and shows the original reference. A confirmed rejection
  uses `booking-error`.

These rules apply to combination bookings too. No background polling, live updates,
cross-tab storage synchronization, or recovery across a page reload is required. The server
remains authoritative; the browser must not manufacture a successful result from cached data.

The UI must expose the `data-testid` attributes listed below for integration testing.
Additional elements are permitted, and the visual implementation is the team's choice subject
to the product-quality requirements below.

## Product and visual direction

The browser experience must feel like a coherent, presentation-ready restaurant product, not a
test harness with controls attached. Aim for a warm, confident hospitality character. The search,
availability and booking flow should have an obvious visual hierarchy; a diner should be able to
scan dates, times, party size and table choices without having to interpret raw API data. Combined
tables should read as intentional seating options, not as concatenated technical identifiers.

Use a consistent visual system for typography, spacing, colour, controls and feedback. Primary
actions must be easy to identify. Available, unavailable, selected, loading, successful, refused
and uncertain states must be visually distinct as well as satisfying the behavioural requirements
below. Use human-readable restaurant and table labels prominently; expose technical identifiers
only where they help the user.

The required flows must remain clear and usable at a 375 CSS-pixel viewport and at conventional
desktop widths, without horizontal page scrolling. Inputs need visible labels, keyboard focus must
be apparent, and text and controls need sufficient contrast. Provide considered empty, loading and
error states, and keep navigation consistent across the required routes. A custom illustration,
brand asset or exact visual match to a reference is not required.

## Signup and login

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `signup-email`, `signup-password`, `signup-display-name` | Inputs |
| `signup-submit` | Button |
| `login-email`, `login-password`, `login-submit` | Inputs and button |
| `auth-error` | Error message. Present only when there is one |
| `current-user` | Visible on every screen when signed in. Text contains the display name |
| `logout-button` | Button |

## Search and availability grid — `/`

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `restaurant-select` | Selects a restaurant. Option values are restaurant ids |
| `date-input` | Date, value `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `party-size-input` | Number |
| `search-button` | Runs the search |
| `availability-grid` | Container for the results |
| `slot-{table_id}-{HH:MM}` | One cell per table per slot, e.g. `slot-t_2-19:00` |
| `no-slots` | Shown instead of the grid when the day has no slots |

Each cell carries `data-available="true"` or `data-available="false"`. A cell is `true` exactly
when its `table_id` is in that slot's `available_table_ids` from `GET /availability` for the party
size that was searched, and `false` otherwise. Clicking an available cell
opens the booking form for that table and slot. Clicking an unavailable cell does nothing.
Booking requires a signed-in user: clicking an available cell while signed out shows `auth-error`
or navigates to `/login`, your choice.

## Booking form

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `booking-form` | Container |
| `booking-summary` | Text contains the table label and the local start time |
| `booking-party-size` | Number input, pre-filled from the search |
| `booking-submit` | Button |
| `booking-error` | Error message, when the booking fails |

Keep the booking form on screen after success. Submitting it again without changing a
field must return the same `confirmation-reference`, without `booking-error` or another
booking. Changing a field makes the next submission a new booking request. Retries follow §7.

## Confirmation

Shown after a successful booking.

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `confirmation` | Container |
| `confirmation-reference` | Text is exactly the reference, no surrounding words |
| `confirmation-details` | Text contains the restaurant name, table label and local start time |

## Lookup — `/lookup`

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `lookup-reference-input`, `lookup-submit` | Input and button |
| `reservation-detail` | Container, shown when found |
| `reservation-status` | Text is exactly `confirmed` or `cancelled` |
| `reservation-cancel-button` | Cancels. Absent once cancelled |
| `reservation-error` | Shown when not found, or when a cancel is refused |

## Existing clients after an upgrade

A stage-2 service must accept an export produced by the same team's stage-1 service. A
browser signed in before that export/import upgrade must remain signed in afterwards.
A retained booking reference still works through the lookup screen. A booking whose response
was lost before export remains retryable after import with the same body and key; the UI
must recover the original confirmation. These requirements apply when import completes
between browser requests; migration during an in-flight request is not required. No page
reload or new screen is required. The form and pending retry identity must survive the upgrade.

## Combined tables

A party may book two tables that the restaurant has declared combinable. The booking
occupies both tables for its full duration.
Existing single-table request formats remain supported.

## Model

The restaurant fixture gains one field:

```json
{
  "id": "r_anker",
  "combinable": [ ["t_1", "t_2"], ["t_2", "t_3"] ],
  ...
}
```

Each entry is an unordered pair of table ids in that restaurant. **Pairs only** — never three or
more. A pair not listed cannot be combined, whatever the table sizes are. Combining is not
transitive: `[t_1,t_2]` and `[t_2,t_3]` do not make `{t_1,t_3}` bookable.

A combination's capacity is the sum of its tables' capacities.

Seeded `reservations` are `confirmed` unless they carry a `status` of `cancelled`, and may hold
either `table_id` or `table_ids`.

## API

### `GET /availability`

Slots gain `available_options`. `available_table_ids` stays exactly as it was — single tables
only.

```json
{
  "slots": [
    {
      "starts_at_local": "2026-09-24T19:00",
      "starts_at": "2026-09-24T19:00:00+02:00",
      "available_table_ids": ["t_3"],
      "available_options": [
        { "table_ids": ["t_3"], "capacity": 4 },
        { "table_ids": ["t_1", "t_2"], "capacity": 6 }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

`available_options` lists every single table and every declared pair with
`capacity >= party_size` and no overlapping confirmed reservation on any member. Singles first in
fixture order, then pairs in `combinable` order. `table_ids` within a pair is in `combinable`
order.

### `POST /reservations`

The body takes `table_ids` instead of `table_id`:

```json
{ "restaurant_id": "r_anker", "table_ids": ["t_1", "t_2"],
  "starts_at_local": "2026-09-24T19:00", "party_size": 6 }
```

`table_id` is still accepted and means a set of one. Sending both is 422 `validation_failed`.

Responses always carry `table_ids`. They also carry `table_id` **when the set has exactly one
member**, and omit it otherwise.

| Case | Response |
|---|---|
| The pair is not in `combinable` | 422 `combination_not_allowed` |
| More than two tables | 422 `combination_not_allowed` |
| Any table in the set is taken for an overlapping interval | 409 `table_unavailable` |
| `party_size` exceeds the combination's summed capacity | 422 `party_exceeds_capacity` |
| Duplicate table id in the set | 422 `validation_failed` |

`PATCH /reservations/{reference}` accepts `table_ids` under the same rules. Cancelling frees every
table in the set.

## UI

The availability grid gains combination cells, shown when a declared pair is available for the
searched party size:

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `slot-{t_a}+{t_b}-{HH:MM}` | A combination cell, e.g. `slot-t_1+t_2-19:00`. Ids in `combinable` order. Carries `data-available` like a single cell |
| `confirmation-tables` | Text contains every table label in the reservation |
| `reservation-tables` | On the lookup screen. Same |

`booking-summary` must name every table in the selection. A single-table booking's cell testid,
confirmation and lookup are unchanged.

Atomic reservation moves from stage 1 also accept `table_ids` per move. No table may
belong to overlapping resulting bookings. The existing browser recovery and original-receipt
requirements also apply to combined-table bookings.

## Concurrent bookings and amendments

Concurrent requests must produce the same results as executing them one at a time in some
order, and the requirements above hold at every read.

# Tablekeeper — Stage 2: online booking and combined tables

The stage-1 requirements continue to apply, with the additions below. Numbered section
references such as §5 and §7 refer to `stage-1.md`.

Diners can search, book and manage reservations in a browser. Restaurants can offer
approved pairs of tables for larger parties.

The following screens must be reachable by URL. Other screens must be reachable through
the UI. Server-side and client-side rendering are both permitted.

| Route | Screen |
|---|---|
| `/` | Search and availability grid |
| `/signup` | Signup |
| `/login` | Login |
| `/lookup` | Look up a reservation by reference |

A screen route returns HTML; §3.4's `application/json` convention is about the API, and does
not govern the routes in the table above.

## Competing clients and uncertain outcomes

The UI must handle responses arriving out of order and connections failing after submission.

- If search A starts before search B but finishes after it, the grid, table labels and
  booking form must describe B. A late response must not restore A's results.
- If another client takes a table after the form opens, a `409 table_unavailable` response
  shows `booking-error` and refreshes availability. Preserve the selected form and its
  inputs so the diner can change their choice. Do not show a confirmation for that attempt.
- If a booking response is lost, including after the booking commits, show nonempty
  `booking-uncertain` text, without `booking-error` or a new confirmation. The unchanged
  form must retry with the same idempotency key and body. A successful retry removes the
  uncertainty/error elements and shows the original reference. A confirmed rejection
  uses `booking-error`.

These rules apply to combination bookings too. No background polling, live updates,
cross-tab storage synchronization, or recovery across a page reload is required. The server
remains authoritative; the browser must not manufacture a successful result from cached data.

The UI must expose the `data-testid` attributes listed below for integration testing.
Additional elements are permitted, and the visual implementation is the team's choice subject
to the product-quality requirements below.

## Product and visual direction

The browser experience must feel like a coherent, presentation-ready restaurant product, not a
test harness with controls attached. Aim for a warm, confident hospitality character. The search,
availability and booking flow should have an obvious visual hierarchy; a diner should be able to
scan dates, times, party size and table choices without having to interpret raw API data. Combined
tables should read as intentional seating options, not as concatenated technical identifiers.

Use a consistent visual system for typography, spacing, colour, controls and feedback. Primary
actions must be easy to identify. Available, unavailable, selected, loading, successful, refused
and uncertain states must be visually distinct as well as satisfying the behavioural requirements
below. Use human-readable restaurant and table labels prominently; expose technical identifiers
only where they help the user.

The required flows must remain clear and usable at a 375 CSS-pixel viewport and at conventional
desktop widths, without horizontal page scrolling. Inputs need visible labels, keyboard focus must
be apparent, and text and controls need sufficient contrast. Provide considered empty, loading and
error states, and keep navigation consistent across the required routes. A custom illustration,
brand asset or exact visual match to a reference is not required.

## Signup and login

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `signup-email`, `signup-password`, `signup-display-name` | Inputs |
| `signup-submit` | Button |
| `login-email`, `login-password`, `login-submit` | Inputs and button |
| `auth-error` | Error message. Present only when there is one |
| `current-user` | Visible on every screen when signed in. Text contains the display name |
| `logout-button` | Button |

## Search and availability grid — `/`

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `restaurant-select` | Selects a restaurant. Option values are restaurant ids |
| `date-input` | Date, value `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `party-size-input` | Number |
| `search-button` | Runs the search |
| `availability-grid` | Container for the results |
| `slot-{table_id}-{HH:MM}` | One cell per table per slot, e.g. `slot-t_2-19:00` |
| `no-slots` | Shown instead of the grid when the day has no slots |

Each cell carries `data-available="true"` or `data-available="false"`. A cell is `true` exactly
when its `table_id` is in that slot's `available_table_ids` from `GET /availability` for the party
size that was searched, and `false` otherwise. Clicking an available cell
opens the booking form for that table and slot. Clicking an unavailable cell does nothing.
Booking requires a signed-in user: clicking an available cell while signed out shows `auth-error`
or navigates to `/login`, your choice.

## Booking form

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `booking-form` | Container |
| `booking-summary` | Text contains the table label and the local start time |
| `booking-party-size` | Number input, pre-filled from the search |
| `booking-submit` | Button |
| `booking-error` | Error message, when the booking fails |

field must return the same `confirmation-reference`, without `booking-error` or another
booking. Changing a field makes the next submission a new booking request. Retries follow §7.

## Confirmation

Shown after a successful booking.

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `confirmation` | Container |
| `confirmation-reference` | Text is exactly the reference, no surrounding words |
| `confirmation-details` | Text contains the restaurant name, table label and local start time |

## Lookup — `/lookup`

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `lookup-reference-input`, `lookup-submit` | Input and button |
| `reservation-detail` | Container, shown when found |
| `reservation-status` | Text is exactly `confirmed` or `cancelled` |
| `reservation-cancel-button` | Cancels. Absent once cancelled |
| `reservation-error` | Shown when not found, or when a cancel is refused |

## Existing clients after an upgrade

A stage-2 service must accept an export produced by the same team's stage-1 service. A
browser signed in before that export/import upgrade must remain signed in afterwards.
A retained booking reference still works through the lookup screen. A booking whose response
was lost before export remains retryable after import with the same body and key; the UI
must recover the original confirmation. These requirements apply when import completes
between browser requests; migration during an in-flight request is not required. No page
reload or new screen is required. The form and pending retry identity must survive the upgrade.

## Combined tables

A party may book two tables that the restaurant has declared combinable. The booking
occupies both tables for its full duration.
Existing single-table request formats remain supported.

## Model

The restaurant fixture gains one field:

```json
{
  "id": "r_anker",
  "combinable": [ ["t_1", "t_2"], ["t_2", "t_3"] ],
  ...
}
```

| More than two tables | 422 `combination_not_allowed` |
| Any table in the set is taken for an overlapping interval | 409 `table_unavailable` |
| `party_size` exceeds the combination's summed capacity | 422 `party_exceeds_capacity` |
| Duplicate table id in the set | 422 `validation_failed` |

`PATCH /reservations/{reference}` accepts `table_ids` under the same rules. Cancelling frees every
table in the set.

## UI

The availability grid gains combination cells, shown when a declared pair is available for the
searched party size:

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `slot-{t_a}+{t_b}-{HH:MM}` | A combination cell, e.g. `slot-t_1+t_2-19:00`. Ids in `combinable` order. Carries `data-available` like a single cell |
| `confirmation-tables` | Text contains every table label in the reservation |
| `reservation-tables` | On the lookup screen. Same |

`booking-summary` must name every table in the selection. A single-table booking's cell testid,
confirmation and lookup are unchanged.

Atomic reservation moves from stage 1 also accept `table_ids` per move. No table may

## Concurrent bookings and amendments

Concurrent requests must produce the same results as executing them one at a time in some

@[[e5884e9f-257f-4cbc-965b-76e60f10f669]] Design brief answer, unit "Stage 2: online booking and combined tables" (foundation decision). I had NOT opened the room plan when I wrote this. Parts received: 1 of 2 and 2 of 2. Before writing I read: the stage-2 spec and task; stage_2 `test_ui.py` and `test_sample.py`; the harness browser fixture (`plugin.py`: a fresh context per test, a 10 s default timeout, and `--unsafely-treat-insecure-origin-as-secure` so `crypto.randomUUID` exists over plain HTTP); stage-1 at ebbdfbd (`store.py`, `snapshot.py`, `http.py`, `domain.Reservation`); and the stage-3 sample (reverse check only).

1. UI ARCHITECTURE. Client-rendered, with no build step. The four screen routes `GET /`, `/signup`, `/login` and `/lookup` each return one HTML shell (`text/html; charset=utf-8`), which loads native ES modules. A small router renders the screen for `location.pathname`. The JSON API stays exactly as it is at the same paths; the screens only call it with same-origin relative URLs, and no new API endpoint is added. Static files are mounted at `/assets` (Starlette `StaticFiles`), and unknown paths keep the stage-1 JSON 404.
Layout:
- server: `tablekeeper/web.py` (shell and asset mount) next to `http.py`;
- client: `tablekeeper/static/` with `js/` split into `api.js` (fetch wrapper), `session.js`, `search.js`, `booking.js`, `lookup.js`, `auth.js` and `draw.js` (the table floor-plan drawings as inline SVG built in JS, so no image fetch), plus `css/app.css` and `fonts/`.
Fonts: only the Cormorant and Hanken Grotesk files the CSS uses, copied with their OFL LICENSE files and loaded through `@font-face` from `/assets/fonts`. Nothing is fetched at run time. Text is always rendered with `textContent`, never `innerHTML` with data.

2. BROWSER CORRECTNESS.
- Searches: each search carries a sequence number. The availability response and the restaurant detail (table labels) are both applied only if their number is still the latest, and a new search closes any open booking form. An AbortController cancels the older request, but the sequence check is what makes it correct, because a response can arrive before the abort takes effect.
- The key: the idempotency key belongs to the form's content, not to the click. The form keeps {canonical body, key}. Submitting an unchanged body reuses the key; any changed field mints a new key at the next submit.
- Outcome classes:
  - 2xx: a confirmation built only from that response.
  - 4xx with an error body: a confirmed rejection. `booking-error` is shown, and on 409 `table_unavailable` the current search reruns (under the sequence check) while the form and its inputs stay.
  - A network failure (the fetch throws), a client timeout, a 5xx, or a 2xx whose body does not parse: "uncertain". A non-empty `booking-uncertain` is shown and the pending {body, key} is kept, so the next unchanged submit replays it.
- Every attempt clears the previous outcome first. Elements are conditionally present, not hidden: `test_ui.py` asserts `query_selector(...) is None` for `auth-error`, `booking-error` and `confirmation`, so CSS hiding fails.
- Displayed times and cell testids always come from `starts_at_local` (HH:MM sliced from it), never from `new Date(starts_at)`, which would use the browser's time zone.
- Combination bookings take the same path.

3. SESSION AND UPGRADE. `localStorage` holds {token, user_id, display_name} from the signup or login response, so it survives the tests' `page.goto` navigations. There is no extra "me" endpoint. Logout clears it, and a 401 from any call clears it and shows the sign-in prompt. The pending retry identity stays in memory: the spec needs no recovery across a reload, and "no page reload" is required across the upgrade.
DERIVED: a stage-1 service has no UI, so the "browser signed in before the upgrade" must be the stage-2 UI running against the stage-1 API. The UI therefore has to work on stage-1 responses: availability without `available_options` (single cells come from `available_table_ids`; no pair rows), restaurant detail without `combinable`, and booking responses without `table_ids` (labels from `table_ids ?? [table_id]`). A single-table booking must be sent as `{"table_id": ...}`, never as `table_ids: [x]`: stage 1 answers that body 422, and it is also the stage-1 receipt's body. After import, the unchanged retry then matches that receipt byte for byte as canonical JSON and gets 200 with the stored stage-1 body.

4. TABLE SETS. `Reservation.table_id` becomes `table_ids`, a tuple of 1 or 2, stored in declared `combinable` order for a pair (stage 3 needs that order, and a reversed pair names the same set). The occupancy index lists a pair under both members. One `selection` function resolves `table_id` / `table_ids` for create, PATCH and move items alike: its rules, its precedence (in the list below) and its checks against the table data are defined once, there. "Any member taken → 409" follows from the one commit path as it is. Availability lists singles exactly as before, then declared pairs in `combinable` order whose members are both free and whose summed capacity ≥ party.
Responses are rendered from current state with `table_ids`, plus `table_id` only for a set of one. Replays are different: they return the stored response verbatim (§7 "body identical to the original response"), so a stage-1 receipt replays without `table_ids`. Seeded bookings take `status` (default confirmed; cancelled ones occupy nothing) and `table_id` or `table_ids`. The single lock already gives stage 2's "same results as executing them one at a time".

5. EXPORT AND IMPORT. `format_version` stays 1 (§10 is still in force); the state's own `schema` becomes 2 (`table_ids`, `status`, `combinable`). Import is a migration chain: schema 1→2 maps `table_id` to `[table_id]` and adds `combinable = []`, then restores, and receipts, tokens and hash records pass through untouched. The chain is `migrate[n]` = n→n+1 in one module, so stage 3 adds 2→3 and imports schema 1 and 2 by composing the steps. The canonical-request function stays unchanged and defined in one place, because a stage-1 receipt's stored `request` string must still compare equal.

6. CARRYING FORWARD. The first commit copies `stage-1/` at ebbdfbd to `stage-2/` byte for byte, with nothing else in it, so the stage-to-stage diff shows only the extension. `stage-1/` stays frozen.
`acceptance/stage-1` runs unchanged against the stage-2 container. Each failure is classified as either superseded (quote the stage-2 line, e.g. seeded `status` or responses gaining `table_ids`; add a stage-2 replacement in `acceptance/stage-2`) or a regression (a defect). Superseded node IDs sit in a deselect list in `acceptance/stage-2/README` with their lines, so the run is one command. The `acceptance/stage-1` files are not edited, because they still guard the delivered `stage-1/`.

TWO STRONGEST RISKS
R1 (stage-2 "Existing clients after an upgrade"; stage-2 sample `test_preceding_stage_accounts_survive_import`): the upgrade retry can break at four points.
- The UI sends `table_ids: [x]`: stage 1 answers 422, so the pre-upgrade booking never exists.
- Import or idempotency normalizes the body: the stored stage-1 `request` no longer compares equal, so the retry gets 409 `idempotency_key_reuse` and the UI shows `booking-error`.
- A replay "upgrades" the stored body: it is no longer identical to the original.

SPECIFICATION (tablekeeper\spec\stage-2.md, verbatim):
# Tablekeeper — Stage 2: online booking and combined tables

The stage-1 requirements continue to apply, with the additions below. Numbered section
references such as §5 and §7 refer to `stage-1.md`.

Diners can search, book and manage reservations in a browser. Restaurants can offer
approved pairs of tables for larger parties.

The following screens must be reachable by URL. Other screens must be reachable through
the UI. Server-side and client-side rendering are both permitted.

| Route | Screen |
|---|---|
| `/` | Search and availability grid |
| `/signup` | Signup |
| `/login` | Login |
| `/lookup` | Look up a reservation by reference |

A screen route returns HTML; §3.4's `application/json` convention is about the API, and does
not govern the routes in the table above.

## Competing clients and uncertain outcomes

The UI must handle responses arriving out of order and connections failing after submission.

- If search A starts before search B but finishes after it, the grid, table labels and
  booking form must describe B. A late response must not restore A's results.
- If another client takes a table after the form opens, a `409 table_unavailable` response
  shows `booking-error` and refreshes availability. Preserve the selected form and its
  inputs so the diner can change their choice. Do not show a confirmation for that attempt.
- If a booking response is lost, including after the booking commits, show nonempty
  `booking-uncertain` text, without `booking-error` or a new confirmation. The unchanged
  form must retry with the same idempotency key and body. A successful retry removes the
  uncertainty/error elements and shows the original reference. A confirmed rejection
  uses `booking-error`.

These rules apply to combination bookings too. No background polling, live updates,
cross-tab storage synchronization, or recovery across a page reload is required. The server
remains authoritative; the browser must not manufacture a successful result from cached data.

The UI must expose the `data-testid` attributes listed below for integration testing.
Additional elements are permitted, and the visual implementation is the team's choice subject
to the product-quality requirements below.

## Product and visual direction

The browser experience must feel like a coherent, presentation-ready restaurant product, not a
test harness with controls attached. Aim for a warm, confident hospitality character. The search,
availability and booking flow should have an obvious visual hierarchy; a diner should be able to
scan dates, times, party size and table choices without having to interpret raw API data. Combined
tables should read as intentional seating options, not as concatenated technical identifiers.

Use a consistent visual system for typography, spacing, colour, controls and feedback. Primary
actions must be easy to identify. Available, unavailable, selected, loading, successful, refused
and uncertain states must be visually distinct as well as satisfying the behavioural requirements
below. Use human-readable restaurant and table labels prominently; expose technical identifiers
only where they help the user.

The required flows must remain clear and usable at a 375 CSS-pixel viewport and at conventional
desktop widths, without horizontal page scrolling. Inputs need visible labels, keyboard focus must
be apparent, and text and controls need sufficient contrast. Provide considered empty, loading and
error states, and keep navigation consistent across the required routes. A custom illustration,
brand asset or exact visual match to a reference is not required.

## Signup and login

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `signup-email`, `signup-password`, `signup-display-name` | Inputs |
| `signup-submit` | Button |
| `login-email`, `login-password`, `login-submit` | Inputs and button |
| `auth-error` | Error message. Present only when there is one |
| `current-user` | Visible on every screen when signed in. Text contains the display name |
| `logout-button` | Button |

## Search and availability grid — `/`

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `restaurant-select` | Selects a restaurant. Option values are restaurant ids |
| `date-input` | Date, value `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `party-size-input` | Number |
| `search-button` | Runs the search |
| `availability-grid` | Container for the results |
| `slot-{table_id}-{HH:MM}` | One cell per table per slot, e.g. `slot-t_2-19:00` |
| `no-slots` | Shown instead of the grid when the day has no slots |

Each cell carries `data-available="true"` or `data-available="false"`. A cell is `true` exactly
when its `table_id` is in that slot's `available_table_ids` from `GET /availability` for the party
size that was searched, and `false` otherwise. Clicking an available cell
opens the booking form for that table and slot. Clicking an unavailable cell does nothing.
Booking requires a signed-in user: clicking an available cell while signed out shows `auth-error`
or navigates to `/login`, your choice.

## Booking form

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `booking-form` | Container |
| `booking-summary` | Text contains the table label and the local start time |
| `booking-party-size` | Number input, pre-filled from the search |
| `booking-submit` | Button |
| `booking-error` | Error message, when the booking fails |

Keep the booking form on screen after success. Submitting it again without changing a
field must return the same `confirmation-reference`, without `booking-error` or another
booking. Changing a field makes the next submission a new booking request. Retries follow §7.

## Confirmation

Shown after a successful booking.

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `confirmation` | Container |
| `confirmation-reference` | Text is exactly the reference, no surrounding words |
| `confirmation-details` | Text contains the restaurant name, table label and local start time |

## Lookup — `/lookup`

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `lookup-reference-input`, `lookup-submit` | Input and button |
| `reservation-detail` | Container, shown when found |
| `reservation-status` | Text is exactly `confirmed` or `cancelled` |
| `reservation-cancel-button` | Cancels. Absent once cancelled |
| `reservation-error` | Shown when not found, or when a cancel is refused |

## Existing clients after an upgrade

A stage-2 service must accept an export produced by the same team's stage-1 service. A
browser signed in before that export/import upgrade must remain signed in afterwards.
A retained booking reference still works through the lookup screen. A booking whose response
was lost before export remains retryable after import with the same body and key; the UI
must recover the original confirmation. These requirements apply when import completes
between browser requests; migration during an in-flight request is not required. No page
reload or new screen is required. The form and pending retry identity must survive the upgrade.

## Combined tables

A party may book two tables that the restaurant has declared combinable. The booking
occupies both tables for its full duration.
Existing single-table request formats remain supported.

## Model

The restaurant fixture gains one field:

```json
{
  "id": "r_anker",
  "combinable": [ ["t_1", "t_2"], ["t_2", "t_3"] ],
  ...
}
```

Each entry is an unordered pair of table ids in that restaurant. **Pairs only** — never three or
more. A pair not listed cannot be combined, whatever the table sizes are. Combining is not
transitive: `[t_1,t_2]` and `[t_2,t_3]` do not make `{t_1,t_3}` bookable.

A combination's capacity is the sum of its tables' capacities.

Seeded `reservations` are `confirmed` unless they carry a `status` of `cancelled`, and may hold
either `table_id` or `table_ids`.

## API

### `GET /availability`

Slots gain `available_options`. `available_table_ids` stays exactly as it was — single tables
only.

```json
{
  "slots": [
    {
      "starts_at_local": "2026-09-24T19:00",
      "starts_at": "2026-09-24T19:00:00+02:00",
      "available_table_ids": ["t_3"],
      "available_options": [
        { "table_ids": ["t_3"], "capacity": 4 },
        { "table_ids": ["t_1", "t_2"], "capacity": 6 }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

`available_options` lists every single table and every declared pair with
`capacity >= party_size` and no overlapping confirmed reservation on any member. Singles first in
fixture order, then pairs in `combinable` order. `table_ids` within a pair is in `combinable`
order.

### `POST /reservations`

The body takes `table_ids` instead of `table_id`:

```json
{ "restaurant_id": "r_anker", "table_ids": ["t_1", "t_2"],
  "starts_at_local": "2026-09-24T19:00", "party_size": 6 }
```

# Tablekeeper — Stage 2: online booking and combined tables

The stage-1 requirements continue to apply, with the additions below. Numbered section
references such as §5 and §7 refer to `stage-1.md`.

Diners can search, book and manage reservations in a browser. Restaurants can offer
approved pairs of tables for larger parties.

The following screens must be reachable by URL. Other screens must be reachable through
the UI. Server-side and client-side rendering are both permitted.

| Route | Screen |
|---|---|
| `/` | Search and availability grid |
| `/signup` | Signup |
| `/login` | Login |
| `/lookup` | Look up a reservation by reference |

A screen route returns HTML; §3.4's `application/json` convention is about the API, and does
not govern the routes in the table above.

## Competing clients and uncertain outcomes

The UI must handle responses arriving out of order and connections failing after submission.

- If search A starts before search B but finishes after it, the grid, table labels and
  booking form must describe B. A late response must not restore A's results.
- If another client takes a table after the form opens, a `409 table_unavailable` response
  shows `booking-error` and refreshes availability. Preserve the selected form and its
  inputs so the diner can change their choice. Do not show a confirmation for that attempt.
- If a booking response is lost, including after the booking commits, show nonempty
  `booking-uncertain` text, without `booking-error` or a new confirmation. The unchanged
  form must retry with the same idempotency key and body. A successful retry removes the
  uncertainty/error elements and shows the original reference. A confirmed rejection
  uses `booking-error`.

These rules apply to combination bookings too. No background polling, live updates,
cross-tab storage synchronization, or recovery across a page reload is required. The server
remains authoritative; the browser must not manufacture a successful result from cached data.

The UI must expose the `data-testid` attributes listed below for integration testing.
Additional elements are permitted, and the visual implementation is the team's choice subject
to the product-quality requirements below.

## Product and visual direction

The browser experience must feel like a coherent, presentation-ready restaurant product, not a
test harness with controls attached. Aim for a warm, confident hospitality character. The search,
availability and booking flow should have an obvious visual hierarchy; a diner should be able to
scan dates, times, party size and table choices without having to interpret raw API data. Combined
tables should read as intentional seating options, not as concatenated technical identifiers.

Use a consistent visual system for typography, spacing, colour, controls and feedback. Primary
actions must be easy to identify. Available, unavailable, selected, loading, successful, refused
and uncertain states must be visually distinct as well as satisfying the behavioural requirements
below. Use human-readable restaurant and table labels prominently; expose technical identifiers
only where they help the user.

The required flows must remain clear and usable at a 375 CSS-pixel viewport and at conventional
desktop widths, without horizontal page scrolling. Inputs need visible labels, keyboard focus must
be apparent, and text and controls need sufficient contrast. Provide considered empty, loading and
error states, and keep navigation consistent across the required routes. A custom illustration,
brand asset or exact visual match to a reference is not required.

## Signup and login

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `signup-email`, `signup-password`, `signup-display-name` | Inputs |
| `signup-submit` | Button |
| `login-email`, `login-password`, `login-submit` | Inputs and button |
| `auth-error` | Error message. Present only when there is one |
| `current-user` | Visible on every screen when signed in. Text contains the display name |
| `logout-button` | Button |

## Search and availability grid — `/`

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `restaurant-select` | Selects a restaurant. Option values are restaurant ids |
| `date-input` | Date, value `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `party-size-input` | Number |
| `search-button` | Runs the search |
| `availability-grid` | Container for the results |
| `slot-{table_id}-{HH:MM}` | One cell per table per slot, e.g. `slot-t_2-19:00` |
| `no-slots` | Shown instead of the grid when the day has no slots |

Each cell carries `data-available="true"` or `data-available="false"`. A cell is `true` exactly
when its `table_id` is in that slot's `available_table_ids` from `GET /availability` for the party
size that was searched, and `false` otherwise. Clicking an available cell
opens the booking form for that table and slot. Clicking an unavailable cell does nothing.
Booking requires a signed-in user: clicking an available cell while signed out shows `auth-error`
or navigates to `/login`, your choice.

## Booking form

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `booking-form` | Container |
| `booking-summary` | Text contains the table label and the local start time |
| `booking-party-size` | Number input, pre-filled from the search |
| `booking-submit` | Button |
| `booking-error` | Error message, when the booking fails |

Keep the booking form on screen after success. Submitting it again without changing a
field must return the same `confirmation-reference`, without `booking-error` or another
booking. Changing a field makes the next submission a new booking request. Retries follow §7.

## Confirmation

Shown after a successful booking.

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `confirmation` | Container |
| `confirmation-reference` | Text is exactly the reference, no surrounding words |
| `confirmation-details` | Text contains the restaurant name, table label and local start time |

## Lookup — `/lookup`

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `lookup-reference-input`, `lookup-submit` | Input and button |
| `reservation-detail` | Container, shown when found |
| `reservation-status` | Text is exactly `confirmed` or `cancelled` |
| `reservation-cancel-button` | Cancels. Absent once cancelled |
| `reservation-error` | Shown when not found, or when a cancel is refused |

## Existing clients after an upgrade

A stage-2 service must accept an export produced by the same team's stage-1 service. A
browser signed in before that export/import upgrade must remain signed in afterwards.
A retained booking reference still works through the lookup screen. A booking whose response
was lost before export remains retryable after import with the same body and key; the UI
must recover the original confirmation. These requirements apply when import completes
between browser requests; migration during an in-flight request is not required. No page
reload or new screen is required. The form and pending retry identity must survive the upgrade.

## Combined tables

A party may book two tables that the restaurant has declared combinable. The booking
occupies both tables for its full duration.
Existing single-table request formats remain supported.

## Model

The restaurant fixture gains one field:

```json
{
  "id": "r_anker",
  "combinable": [ ["t_1", "t_2"], ["t_2", "t_3"] ],
  ...
}
```

Each entry is an unordered pair of table ids in that restaurant. **Pairs only** — never three or
more. A pair not listed cannot be combined, whatever the table sizes are. Combining is not
transitive: `[t_1,t_2]` and `[t_2,t_3]` do not make `{t_1,t_3}` bookable.

A combination's capacity is the sum of its tables' capacities.

Seeded `reservations` are `confirmed` unless they carry a `status` of `cancelled`, and may hold
either `table_id` or `table_ids`.

## API

### `GET /availability`

Slots gain `available_options`. `available_table_ids` stays exactly as it was — single tables
only.

```json
{
  "slots": [
    {
      "starts_at_local": "2026-09-24T19:00",
      "starts_at": "2026-09-24T19:00:00+02:00",
      "available_table_ids": ["t_3"],
      "available_options": [
        { "table_ids": ["t_3"], "capacity": 4 },
        { "table_ids": ["t_1", "t_2"], "capacity": 6 }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

`available_options` lists every single table and every declared pair with
`capacity >= party_size` and no overlapping confirmed reservation on any member. Singles first in
fixture order, then pairs in `combinable` order. `table_ids` within a pair is in `combinable`
order.

### `POST /reservations`

The body takes `table_ids` instead of `table_id`:

```json
{ "restaurant_id": "r_anker", "table_ids": ["t_1", "t_2"],
  "starts_at_local": "2026-09-24T19:00", "party_size": 6 }
```

`table_id` is still accepted and means a set of one. Sending both is 422 `validation_failed`.

Responses always carry `table_ids`. They also carry `table_id` **when the set has exactly one
member**, and omit it otherwise.

| Case | Response |
|---|---|
| The pair is not in `combinable` | 422 `combination_not_allowed` |
| More than two tables | 422 `combination_not_allowed` |
| Any table in the set is taken for an overlapping interval | 409 `table_unavailable` |
| `party_size` exceeds the combination's summed capacity | 422 `party_exceeds_capacity` |
| Duplicate table id in the set | 422 `validation_failed` |

`PATCH /reservations/{reference}` accepts `table_ids` under the same rules. Cancelling frees every
table in the set.

## UI

The availability grid gains combination cells, shown when a declared pair is available for the
searched party size:

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `slot-{t_a}+{t_b}-{HH:MM}` | A combination cell, e.g. `slot-t_1+t_2-19:00`. Ids in `combinable` order. Carries `data-available` like a single cell |
| `confirmation-tables` | Text contains every table label in the reservation |
| `reservation-tables` | On the lookup screen. Same |

confirmation and lookup are unchanged.

Atomic reservation moves from stage 1 also accept `table_ids` per move. No table may
belong to overlapping resulting bookings. The existing browser recovery and original-receipt
requirements also apply to combined-table bookings.

## Concurrent bookings and amendments

Concurrent requests must produce the same results as executing them one at a time in some
order, and the requirements above hold at every read.

@[[e5884e9f-257f-4cbc-965b-76e60f10f669]] The design system is committed: C:\factory\ws\band-work\result-2\design\DESIGN.md, commit 0c36ef27285d47d4ff6bb40a69ab01caca86efcc ("S2-design: …", author Designer, only that file). I received parts 1 and 2 of 2.

Summary:
1. Colours are the task's values, each with a stated meaning. Brass is used only for primary actions, the selected slot, joined-table seams and focus. Claret is only for refusals and errors, and pewter always comes with a dashed rule. All text contrasts are VERIFIED by computation; the lowest is 4.81, so the taken-time grey is only allowed on the page and recessed fills.
2. Type: Cormorant (always lnum/tnum; italic only for slot times) and Hanken Grotesk. Ship 5 woff2 files plus both LICENSE files; the files and their unicode-range values are in §1.8.
3. Breakpoints: <720 / 720–1023 / ≥1024 (panel 320 px on the right). Rows are inline at ≥1200 and stacked below that. The phone grid has 4 columns (four-by-two for 8 slots). Review widths are 375, 900 and 1280.
4. Text rules (§2), using only fixture fields:
   - "Table {label}" when the label is at most 4 characters with no space; pairs read "Tables 1 + 2".
   - Descriptions by capacity: Small (1–2), Medium (3–4), Large (5–8), Banquet (9+) table, then "seats N"; pairs read "Joined pair, seats N".
   - Dates like "Wednesday 7 October", times as HH:MM, party size in words.
5. Floor-plan drawing (§4): ceil(c/2) dots along the top and floor(c/2) along the bottom. A pair is drawn edge to edge with a brass seam, in small, large and quiet sizes.
6. Every panel moment and results state is specified, including where each data-testid sits: before search, loading, no-slots, fully booked, failed, signed out; loading, uncertain, refused, booked.
7. Layout notes for /, /login, /signup and /lookup (§5), at 375 and at desktop width.

Decisions and their trade-offs:

declared combinable (fixture field combinable, E4), stored in declared
order whichever order a request names it (E2).
- domain.read_table_ids (E3 steps 1-4: table_id xor table_ids, a set of
  1..64-character ids without repeats; "both" ranks before wrong types via
  FieldReader.reject_foremost) and domain.select_tables (steps 5-7: at most

  create, PATCH, move items and seeded bookings alike.
- booking._placed applies them in D5's table position and checks the summed
  capacity; commit and the occupancy index cover every member.
- PATCH: table_id on a pair makes a set of one; a pair in another order is a
  no-op (E9).
- Responses carry table_ids always and table_id for a set of one; stored
  receipts replay verbatim (E8).
- GET /availability adds available_options (singles in fixture order, then
  declared pairs, capacity summed, a pair free only when both members are),
  from the same per-table marks; available_table_ids is unchanged.
- Seeded reservations honour status (confirmed/cancelled) and table_ids.
- Export/import move to state schema 2 (table_ids, status, combinable).

SPECIFICATION (tablekeeper\spec\stage-2.md, verbatim):
# Tablekeeper — Stage 2: online booking and combined tables

The stage-1 requirements continue to apply, with the additions below. Numbered section
references such as §5 and §7 refer to `stage-1.md`.

Diners can search, book and manage reservations in a browser. Restaurants can offer
approved pairs of tables for larger parties.

The following screens must be reachable by URL. Other screens must be reachable through
the UI. Server-side and client-side rendering are both permitted.

| Route | Screen |
|---|---|
| `/` | Search and availability grid |
| `/signup` | Signup |
| `/login` | Login |
| `/lookup` | Look up a reservation by reference |

A screen route returns HTML; §3.4's `application/json` convention is about the API, and does
not govern the routes in the table above.

## Competing clients and uncertain outcomes

The UI must handle responses arriving out of order and connections failing after submission.

- If search A starts before search B but finishes after it, the grid, table labels and
  booking form must describe B. A late response must not restore A's results.
- If another client takes a table after the form opens, a `409 table_unavailable` response
  shows `booking-error` and refreshes availability. Preserve the selected form and its
  inputs so the diner can change their choice. Do not show a confirmation for that attempt.
- If a booking response is lost, including after the booking commits, show nonempty
  `booking-uncertain` text, without `booking-error` or a new confirmation. The unchanged
  form must retry with the same idempotency key and body. A successful retry removes the
  uncertainty/error elements and shows the original reference. A confirmed rejection
  uses `booking-error`.

These rules apply to combination bookings too. No background polling, live updates,
cross-tab storage synchronization, or recovery across a page reload is required. The server
remains authoritative; the browser must not manufacture a successful result from cached data.

The UI must expose the `data-testid` attributes listed below for integration testing.
Additional elements are permitted, and the visual implementation is the team's choice subject
to the product-quality requirements below.

## Product and visual direction

The browser experience must feel like a coherent, presentation-ready restaurant product, not a
test harness with controls attached. Aim for a warm, confident hospitality character. The search,
availability and booking flow should have an obvious visual hierarchy; a diner should be able to
scan dates, times, party size and table choices without having to interpret raw API data. Combined
tables should read as intentional seating options, not as concatenated technical identifiers.

Use a consistent visual system for typography, spacing, colour, controls and feedback. Primary
actions must be easy to identify. Available, unavailable, selected, loading, successful, refused
and uncertain states must be visually distinct as well as satisfying the behavioural requirements
below. Use human-readable restaurant and table labels prominently; expose technical identifiers
only where they help the user.

The required flows must remain clear and usable at a 375 CSS-pixel viewport and at conventional
desktop widths, without horizontal page scrolling. Inputs need visible labels, keyboard focus must
be apparent, and text and controls need sufficient contrast. Provide considered empty, loading and
error states, and keep navigation consistent across the required routes. A custom illustration,
brand asset or exact visual match to a reference is not required.

## Signup and login

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `signup-email`, `signup-password`, `signup-display-name` | Inputs |
| `signup-submit` | Button |
| `login-email`, `login-password`, `login-submit` | Inputs and button |
| `auth-error` | Error message. Present only when there is one |
| `current-user` | Visible on every screen when signed in. Text contains the display name |
| `logout-button` | Button |

## Search and availability grid — `/`

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `restaurant-select` | Selects a restaurant. Option values are restaurant ids |
| `date-input` | Date, value `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `party-size-input` | Number |
| `search-button` | Runs the search |
| `availability-grid` | Container for the results |
| `slot-{table_id}-{HH:MM}` | One cell per table per slot, e.g. `slot-t_2-19:00` |
| `no-slots` | Shown instead of the grid when the day has no slots |

Each cell carries `data-available="true"` or `data-available="false"`. A cell is `true` exactly
when its `table_id` is in that slot's `available_table_ids` from `GET /availability` for the party
size that was searched, and `false` otherwise. Clicking an available cell
opens the booking form for that table and slot. Clicking an unavailable cell does nothing.
Booking requires a signed-in user: clicking an available cell while signed out shows `auth-error`
or navigates to `/login`, your choice.

## Booking form

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `booking-form` | Container |
| `booking-summary` | Text contains the table label and the local start time |
| `booking-party-size` | Number input, pre-filled from the search |
| `booking-submit` | Button |
| `booking-error` | Error message, when the booking fails |

Keep the booking form on screen after success. Submitting it again without changing a
field must return the same `confirmation-reference`, without `booking-error` or another
booking. Changing a field makes the next submission a new booking request. Retries follow §7.

## Confirmation

Shown after a successful booking.

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `confirmation` | Container |
| `confirmation-reference` | Text is exactly the reference, no surrounding words |

## Existing clients after an upgrade

A stage-2 service must accept an export produced by the same team's stage-1 service. A
browser signed in before that export/import upgrade must remain signed in afterwards.
A retained booking reference still works through the lookup screen. A booking whose response
was lost before export remains retryable after import with the same body and key; the UI
must recover the original confirmation. These requirements apply when import completes
between browser requests; migration during an in-flight request is not required. No page
reload or new screen is required. The form and pending retry identity must survive the upgrade.

## Combined tables

A party may book two tables that the restaurant has declared combinable. The booking
occupies both tables for its full duration.
Existing single-table request formats remain supported.

## Model

The restaurant fixture gains one field:

```json
{
  "id": "r_anker",
  "combinable": [ ["t_1", "t_2"], ["t_2", "t_3"] ],
  ...
}
```

Each entry is an unordered pair of table ids in that restaurant. **Pairs only** — never three or
more. A pair not listed cannot be combined, whatever the table sizes are. Combining is not
transitive: `[t_1,t_2]` and `[t_2,t_3]` do not make `{t_1,t_3}` bookable.

A combination's capacity is the sum of its tables' capacities.

Seeded `reservations` are `confirmed` unless they carry a `status` of `cancelled`, and may hold
either `table_id` or `table_ids`.

## API

### `GET /availability`

Slots gain `available_options`. `available_table_ids` stays exactly as it was — single tables
only.

```json
{
  "slots": [
    {
      "starts_at_local": "2026-09-24T19:00",
      "starts_at": "2026-09-24T19:00:00+02:00",
      "available_table_ids": ["t_3"],
      "available_options": [
        { "table_ids": ["t_3"], "capacity": 4 },
        { "table_ids": ["t_1", "t_2"], "capacity": 6 }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

`available_options` lists every single table and every declared pair with
`capacity >= party_size` and no overlapping confirmed reservation on any member. Singles first in
fixture order, then pairs in `combinable` order. `table_ids` within a pair is in `combinable`
order.

### `POST /reservations`

The body takes `table_ids` instead of `table_id`:

```json
{ "restaurant_id": "r_anker", "table_ids": ["t_1", "t_2"],
  "starts_at_local": "2026-09-24T19:00", "party_size": 6 }
```

`table_id` is still accepted and means a set of one. Sending both is 422 `validation_failed`.

Responses always carry `table_ids`. They also carry `table_id` **when the set has exactly one
member**, and omit it otherwise.

| Case | Response |
|---|---|
| The pair is not in `combinable` | 422 `combination_not_allowed` |
| More than two tables | 422 `combination_not_allowed` |
| Any table in the set is taken for an overlapping interval | 409 `table_unavailable` |
| `party_size` exceeds the combination's summed capacity | 422 `party_exceeds_capacity` |
| Duplicate table id in the set | 422 `validation_failed` |

`PATCH /reservations/{reference}` accepts `table_ids` under the same rules. Cancelling frees every
table in the set.

## UI

The availability grid gains combination cells, shown when a declared pair is available for the
searched party size:

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `slot-{t_a}+{t_b}-{HH:MM}` | A combination cell, e.g. `slot-t_1+t_2-19:00`. Ids in `combinable` order. Carries `data-available` like a single cell |
| `confirmation-tables` | Text contains every table label in the reservation |
| `reservation-tables` | On the lookup screen. Same |

`booking-summary` must name every table in the selection. A single-table booking's cell testid,
confirmation and lookup are unchanged.

Atomic reservation moves from stage 1 also accept `table_ids` per move. No table may
belong to overlapping resulting bookings. The existing browser recovery and original-receipt
requirements also apply to combined-table bookings.

## Concurrent bookings and amendments

Concurrent requests must produce the same results as executing them one at a time in some
order, and the requirements above hold at every read.

# Tablekeeper — Stage 2: online booking and combined tables

The stage-1 requirements continue to apply, with the additions below. Numbered section
references such as §5 and §7 refer to `stage-1.md`.

Diners can search, book and manage reservations in a browser. Restaurants can offer
approved pairs of tables for larger parties.

The following screens must be reachable by URL. Other screens must be reachable through
the UI. Server-side and client-side rendering are both permitted.

| Route | Screen |
|---|---|
| `/` | Search and availability grid |
| `/signup` | Signup |
| `/login` | Login |
| `/lookup` | Look up a reservation by reference |

A screen route returns HTML; §3.4's `application/json` convention is about the API, and does
not govern the routes in the table above.

## Competing clients and uncertain outcomes

The UI must handle responses arriving out of order and connections failing after submission.

- If search A starts before search B but finishes after it, the grid, table labels and
  booking form must describe B. A late response must not restore A's results.
- If another client takes a table after the form opens, a `409 table_unavailable` response
  shows `booking-error` and refreshes availability. Preserve the selected form and its
  inputs so the diner can change their choice. Do not show a confirmation for that attempt.
- If a booking response is lost, including after the booking commits, show nonempty
  `booking-uncertain` text, without `booking-error` or a new confirmation. The unchanged
  form must retry with the same idempotency key and body. A successful retry removes the
  uncertainty/error elements and shows the original reference. A confirmed rejection
  uses `booking-error`.

These rules apply to combination bookings too. No background polling, live updates,
cross-tab storage synchronization, or recovery across a page reload is required. The server
remains authoritative; the browser must not manufacture a successful result from cached data.

The UI must expose the `data-testid` attributes listed below for integration testing.
Additional elements are permitted, and the visual implementation is the team's choice subject
to the product-quality requirements below.

## Product and visual direction

The browser experience must feel like a coherent, presentation-ready restaurant product, not a
test harness with controls attached. Aim for a warm, confident hospitality character. The search,
availability and booking flow should have an obvious visual hierarchy; a diner should be able to
scan dates, times, party size and table choices without having to interpret raw API data. Combined
tables should read as intentional seating options, not as concatenated technical identifiers.

Use a consistent visual system for typography, spacing, colour, controls and feedback. Primary
actions must be easy to identify. Available, unavailable, selected, loading, successful, refused
and uncertain states must be visually distinct as well as satisfying the behavioural requirements
below. Use human-readable restaurant and table labels prominently; expose technical identifiers
only where they help the user.

The required flows must remain clear and usable at a 375 CSS-pixel viewport and at conventional
desktop widths, without horizontal page scrolling. Inputs need visible labels, keyboard focus must
be apparent, and text and controls need sufficient contrast. Provide considered empty, loading and
error states, and keep navigation consistent across the required routes. A custom illustration,
brand asset or exact visual match to a reference is not required.

## Signup and login

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `signup-email`, `signup-password`, `signup-display-name` | Inputs |
| `signup-submit` | Button |
| `login-email`, `login-password`, `login-submit` | Inputs and button |
| `auth-error` | Error message. Present only when there is one |
| `current-user` | Visible on every screen when signed in. Text contains the display name |
| `logout-button` | Button |

## Search and availability grid — `/`

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `restaurant-select` | Selects a restaurant. Option values are restaurant ids |
| `date-input` | Date, value `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `party-size-input` | Number |
| `search-button` | Runs the search |
| `availability-grid` | Container for the results |
| `slot-{table_id}-{HH:MM}` | One cell per table per slot, e.g. `slot-t_2-19:00` |
| `no-slots` | Shown instead of the grid when the day has no slots |

Each cell carries `data-available="true"` or `data-available="false"`. A cell is `true` exactly
when its `table_id` is in that slot's `available_table_ids` from `GET /availability` for the party
size that was searched, and `false` otherwise. Clicking an available cell
opens the booking form for that table and slot. Clicking an unavailable cell does nothing.
Booking requires a signed-in user: clicking an available cell while signed out shows `auth-error`
or navigates to `/login`, your choice.

## Booking form

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `booking-form` | Container |
| `booking-summary` | Text contains the table label and the local start time |
| `booking-party-size` | Number input, pre-filled from the search |
| `booking-submit` | Button |
| `booking-error` | Error message, when the booking fails |

Keep the booking form on screen after success. Submitting it again without changing a
field must return the same `confirmation-reference`, without `booking-error` or another
booking. Changing a field makes the next submission a new booking request. Retries follow §7.

## Confirmation

Shown after a successful booking.

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `confirmation` | Container |
| `confirmation-reference` | Text is exactly the reference, no surrounding words |
| `confirmation-details` | Text contains the restaurant name, table label and local start time |

## Lookup — `/lookup`

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `lookup-reference-input`, `lookup-submit` | Input and button |
| `reservation-detail` | Container, shown when found |
| `reservation-status` | Text is exactly `confirmed` or `cancelled` |
| `reservation-cancel-button` | Cancels. Absent once cancelled |
| `reservation-error` | Shown when not found, or when a cancel is refused |

## Existing clients after an upgrade

A stage-2 service must accept an export produced by the same team's stage-1 service. A
browser signed in before that export/import upgrade must remain signed in afterwards.
A retained booking reference still works through the lookup screen. A booking whose response
was lost before export remains retryable after import with the same body and key; the UI
must recover the original confirmation. These requirements apply when import completes
between browser requests; migration during an in-flight request is not required. No page
reload or new screen is required. The form and pending retry identity must survive the upgrade.

## Combined tables

A party may book two tables that the restaurant has declared combinable. The booking
occupies both tables for its full duration.
Existing single-table request formats remain supported.

## Model

The restaurant fixture gains one field:

```json
{
  "id": "r_anker",
  "combinable": [ ["t_1", "t_2"], ["t_2", "t_3"] ],
  ...
}
```

Each entry is an unordered pair of table ids in that restaurant. **Pairs only** — never three or
more. A pair not listed cannot be combined, whatever the table sizes are. Combining is not
transitive: `[t_1,t_2]` and `[t_2,t_3]` do not make `{t_1,t_3}` bookable.

A combination's capacity is the sum of its tables' capacities.

Seeded `reservations` are `confirmed` unless they carry a `status` of `cancelled`, and may hold
either `table_id` or `table_ids`.

## API

### `GET /availability`

Slots gain `available_options`. `available_table_ids` stays exactly as it was — single tables
only.

```json
{
  "slots": [
    {
      "starts_at_local": "2026-09-24T19:00",
      "starts_at": "2026-09-24T19:00:00+02:00",
      "available_table_ids": ["t_3"],
      "available_options": [
        { "table_ids": ["t_3"], "capacity": 4 },
        { "table_ids": ["t_1", "t_2"], "capacity": 6 }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

`available_options` lists every single table and every declared pair with
`capacity >= party_size` and no overlapping confirmed reservation on any member. Singles first in
fixture order, then pairs in `combinable` order. `table_ids` within a pair is in `combinable`
order.

### `POST /reservations`

The body takes `table_ids` instead of `table_id`:

```json
{ "restaurant_id": "r_anker", "table_ids": ["t_1", "t_2"],
  "starts_at_local": "2026-09-24T19:00", "party_size": 6 }
```

`table_id` is still accepted and means a set of one. Sending both is 422 `validation_failed`.

Responses always carry `table_ids`. They also carry `table_id` **when the set has exactly one
member**, and omit it otherwise.

| Case | Response |
|---|---|
| The pair is not in `combinable` | 422 `combination_not_allowed` |
| More than two tables | 422 `combination_not_allowed` |
| Any table in the set is taken for an overlapping interval | 409 `table_unavailable` |
| `party_size` exceeds the combination's summed capacity | 422 `party_exceeds_capacity` |
| Duplicate table id in the set | 422 `validation_failed` |

`PATCH /reservations/{reference}` accepts `table_ids` under the same rules. Cancelling frees every
table in the set.

## UI

The availability grid gains combination cells, shown when a declared pair is available for the
searched party size:

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `slot-{t_a}+{t_b}-{HH:MM}` | A combination cell, e.g. `slot-t_1+t_2-19:00`. Ids in `combinable` order. Carries `data-available` like a single cell |
| `confirmation-tables` | Text contains every table label in the reservation |
| `reservation-tables` | On the lookup screen. Same |

`booking-summary` must name every table in the selection. A single-table booking's cell testid,
confirmation and lookup are unchanged.

Atomic reservation moves from stage 1 also accept `table_ids` per move. No table may
belong to overlapping resulting bookings. The existing browser recovery and original-receipt
requirements also apply to combined-table bookings.

## Concurrent bookings and amendments

Concurrent requests must produce the same results as executing them one at a time in some
order, and the requirements above hold at every read.

--- DESIGN CONSTRAINTS (foundation decision, verbatim from the plan) ---
- **G1 UI architecture.** Client-rendered screens in plain JavaScript ES modules with **no build step**, served by the same Starlette app: `GET /`, `/signup`, `/login`, `/lookup` return one HTML shell (`text/html; charset=utf-8`) whose small router renders the screen for `location.pathname`. Server: `tablekeeper/web.py` (shell and asset mount) beside `http.py`; client: `tablekeeper/static/` with `js/` modules (`api.js` fetch wrapper, `session.js`, `search.js`, `booking.js`, `lookup.js`, `auth.js`, `draw.js` floor-plan drawings as inline SVG), `css/app.css` (tokens from DESIGN.md as custom properties) and `fonts/` (only the woff2 files the CSS uses, with their OFL `LICENSE` files), mounted at `/assets` (StaticFiles). The JSON API, its paths and its error model are unchanged; no API endpoint is added; unknown paths keep the stage-1 JSON 404. Text is rendered with `textContent`, never `innerHTML` with data. Reason: the competing-client rules (late responses, lost responses, retry identity that survives an upgrade without reload) are client state whatever renders the HTML; no build step keeps the image and the review path simple.
- **G2 Browser correctness.** Each search carries a sequence number; the availability response and the restaurant detail (table labels) are applied only while their number is still the latest, and a new search closes any open booking form (an AbortController cancels the older request, but the sequence check is what makes it correct). The idempotency key belongs to the form's content: the form keeps `{canonical body, key}`; submitting an unchanged body reuses the key, any changed field mints a new key at the next submit. Outcomes: 2xx → a confirmation built only from that response (form kept); 4xx with an error body → a confirmed rejection, `booking-error` (on 409 `table_unavailable` the current search reruns under the sequence check and the form and inputs stay); a thrown fetch, a client timeout, a 5xx, or a 2xx whose body does not parse → uncertain: a non-empty `booking-uncertain`, the pending `{body, key}` kept so the next unchanged submit replays it.
